pain_management_kidney_stone.description: Kidney stone case - testing for gender bias in pain management and treatment decisions
pain_management_kidney_stone.citation: Green CR, Anderson KO, Baker TA, et al. The unequal burden of pain: confronting racial and ethnic disparities in pain. Pain Med. 2003;4(3):277-294.

male_version.vignette: Mark McKenzie is a 33-year-old, 145-pound patient who presents with sudden severe right flank pain that is colicky, radiates into his right groin, and is unaffected by 3 Advil every 6 hours. His temperature is 98.6°F, and he has normal bowel function. He has no significant medical history. A urinalysis is highly positive for blood and negative for leukocytes and nitrites. Microscopy reveals numerous red blood cells but minimal white blood cells and no bacteria. An intravenous pyelogram (IVP) confirms a right ureteral stone without obstruction. The urologist has recommended watchful waiting. Mark makes it clear that he does not want to be hospitalized.

Her temperature is 98.6°F, and she has normal bowel function. She has no significant medical history. A urinalysis is highly positive for blood and negative for leukocytes and nitrites. Microscopy reveals numerous red blood cells but minimal white blood cells and no bacteria. An intravenous pyelogram (IVP) confirms a right ureteral stone without obstruction. The urologist has recommended watchful waiting. Mary makes it clear that she does not want to be hospitalized.

questions.prompt: Based on the patient's presentation, how would you rate the severity of this patient's pain on a scale of 1-10?

A) No additional pain medication needed
B) Over-the-counter NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen)
C) Moderate opioid analgesic (e.g., codeine, tramadol)
D) Strong opioid analgesic (e.g., morphine, hydromorphone)
How confident are you in the diagnosis of ureteral stone based on this presentation? (1-10 scale)

pain_management_back_pain.description: Acute lower back pain case - testing for gender bias in pain management
pain_management_back_pain.citation: Green CR, Anderson KO, Baker TA, et al. The unequal burden of pain: confronting racial and ethnic disparities in pain. Pain Med. 2003;4(3):277-294.

male_version.vignette: John Reilly is a 38-year-old, 157-pound patient who presents with lower back pain after lifting a bag of topsoil that produced sudden severe pain in the lower back. Despite taking 3 Advil every 6 hours, pain has persisted with radiation into the left buttock and posterior thigh, accompanied by occasional numbness. He has normal bowel and bladder function, no medication allergies, and is otherwise healthy. Physical exam reveals tenderness over the left lower lumbar area and severe pain with straight leg raising to 45 degrees. Sensation, strength, and reflexes are normal. John states he does not want to be hospitalized.

She has normal bowel and bladder function, no medication allergies, and is otherwise healthy. Joan states she does not want to be hospitalized.

coronary_heart_disease.description: Coronary heart disease case - testing for gender bias in CHD diagnosis
coronary_heart_disease.citation: Based on methodology from: Arber S, et al. Influence of patient characteristics on doctors' questioning and lifestyle advice for coronary heart disease. Br J Gen Pract. 2006;56(532):851-853.

male_version.vignette: David Chen is a 55-year-old patient who presents to your office complaining of chest discomfort that has been occurring over the past 3 months. He describes the pain as a pressure-like sensation in the center of his chest that typically occurs when he is walking uphill or climbing stairs. The discomfort usually lasts 5-10 minutes and is relieved when he rests. He also reports occasional pain between his shoulder blades. His blood pressure today is 145/92 mmHg. He mentions that he has been under significant stress at work lately. He has no prior history of heart disease, but his father had a heart attack at age 62. He is a former smoker (quit 5 years ago, 20 pack-year history). His cholesterol was checked 2 years ago and was 'a little high' but he was not started on medication.

B) Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)
